full_judgment: 40. It is true that the condemned-convict obtained bail from the trial Court but, thereafter she absconded and consequently her bail was cancelled. From the above view, she is a fugitive from justice. It cannot be the only ground to pass conviction or to maintain the conviction because she is a fugitive, while the prosecution failed to prove the charge against her beyond any shadow of doubt. Although, her abscondence points the finger at her that she committed the offence, but the suspicion or presumption, whatever its gravity, might be cannot by itself be the basis of conviction, where the prosecution fails to prove the charge against her by legal evidence. In view of the discussion made hereinabove, we find no ground to accept this reference or to sustain the conviction.
